records.title: A finite chiral 4-polytope in R^4 (Roli's cube)
records.authors: J. Bracho, I. Hubard, D. Pellicer
records.venue: Discrete Comput. Geom. 52(4) 799-805; arXiv:1311.1558
records.how_found: arXiv API author query; Crossref reference lists of Pellicer 2021 and McMullen 2021; cited in Monson and Hubard-Schulte
records.relevance: Baseline: the only published finite chiral 4-polytope in E^4 (type {8,3,3}, facet H_0({4,3,3})) found in any database searched.
records.verbatim_quote: arXiv abstract opening: "In this paper, we give an example of a chiral 4-polytope in projective 3-space." Monson (arXiv 2102.08796, p.1): "R is a chiral 4-polytope of type {8,3,3}, faithfully realized in E4 (a situation earlier thought impossible)."

records.title: On Roli's cube
records.venue: The Art of Discrete and Applied Mathematics 5 (2022), no. 3, Paper P3.10, 17 pp. (zbMATH 7612292); arXiv:2102.08796
records.how_found: arXiv API query chiral+polytope; zbMATH API; Semantic Scholar citations of Pellicer 2021
records.relevance: Re-describes Roli's cube, computes minimal regular cover; constructs NO new full-rank chiral polytope. States explicitly that such objects 'seem to be elusive'.
records.theorem_or_page: Introduction p.1; Theorem 6.1 (type {8,3,3}, symmetry group order 192)
records.verbatim_quote: "Chiral polytopes with realizations of `full rank' had (incorrectly) been shown not to exist by Peter McMullen in [11, Theorem 11.2]. Mind you, these objects do seem to be elusive. Pellicer has proved in [15] that chiral polytopes of full rank can exist only in ranks 4 or 5."

records.title: Chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5
records.venue: Beiträge zur Algebra und Geometrie 62 (2021), no. 3, 651-665 (zbMATH 7375630); received 16 Jun 2020, accepted 20 Oct 2020
records.how_found: zbMATH API search 'chiral polytope full rank'; Springer page via cookie redirect; Crossref
records.relevance: Proves the rank restriction; constructs no new rank-4 example. Its reference list contains only Roli's cube (BHP 2014) as a finite full-rank chiral example.
records.theorem_or_page: Abstract; page numbers of theorem not retrieved
records.verbatim_quote: Abstract: "Skeletal chiral polytopes of rank n in a Euclidean space must have as ambient space R^d for some d >= n if they are finite, or some d >= n-1 if they are infinite. If the dimension attains the lower bound just mentioned, we say that the polytope is of full rank. In this article it is proven that a chiral polytope of full rank can only have rank 4 or 5." zbMATH review: "It is known that chiral polytopes of full rank do not exist if n=2 or n=3 and that they do exist for n=4 and n=5."

records.title: A chiral 5-polytope of full rank
records.venue: Discrete Mathematics 344 (2021), no. 6, Paper 112370, 10 pp. (zbMATH 7340595, reviewer R. Schneider)
records.how_found: zbMATH API; Crossref; Google Scholar; ScienceDirect page itself returned HTTP 403
records.relevance: Rank 5, infinite (2-skeleton of {3,4,3,3}); not a rank-4 example. Search snippets attributed to this paper state Roli's cube was the first known full-rank chiral polytope and that all chiral 4-polytopes of full rank are finite.
records.verbatim_quote: zbMATH review: this paper "constructs the first chiral 5-polytope of full rank." WebSearch snippet (source not directly fetched): "The first chiral polytope of full rank known was Roli's cube, a rank 4 polytope discovered in 2014"; "All known chiral 5-polytopes of full rank are infinite, while all chiral 4-polytopes of full rank are finite."
records.confidence: high for bibliography; medium for snippets

records.title: A chiral 4-polytope in R^3
records.venue: Ars Mathematica Contemporanea 12 (2017), no. 2, 315-327 (zbMATH 6774882)
records.how_found: zbMATH API; AMC journal page fetched
records.relevance: Infinite chiral 4-polytope of full rank in E^3 (not E^4). Its abstract confirms that as of 2017 the only finite full-rank chiral example was Roli's cube.
records.verbatim_quote: "In this paper we describe an infinite chiral 4-polytope in the Euclidean 3-space. This builds on previous work of Bracho, Hubard and the author, where a finite chiral 4-polytope in the Euclidean 4-space is constructed. These two polytopes show that there are finite and infinite chiral polytopes of full rank as defined by McMullen."

records.how_found: WebSearch; author-hosted PDF fetched and text-extracted (Springer page blocked by cookie redirect)
records.relevance: Source of the facet claim under audit. The paper itself constructs no 4-polytope; it only asserts H_0({5,3,3}) 'can be taken as facet' and notes H_0({4,3,3}) was used in [3]. Supplementary code/pictures at https://www.matem.unam.mx/~roli/PetrieCoxeter.html. Semantic Scholar lists only one citing work (Hubard-Schulte 2026).
records.theorem_or_page: Section 4; author PDF p.23 (H_0({4,3,3})) and p.25 (H_0({5,3,3})); Theorem 11, Theorem 13, Proposition 14 concern PC_alpha(T)
records.verbatim_quote: p.23: "for alpha = 0 no vertices come together, so we still have a chiral polyhedron H0({4,3,3}), which was taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope in S3 (or R4) in [3]." p.25: "The type of H_alpha({5,3,3}) is {30/(1,11),3}, and for alpha = 0 no vertices identify, so that H0({5,3,3}) can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope, but not H1({5,3,3}) in which four vertices come together."

No master's thesis record found in the UNAM repository (only a 2021 licenciatura thesis 'Las simetrías de las teselaciones en el plano', handle TES01000819758).
records.verbatim_quote: "el estudiante González Casanova trabajó con la Dra. Hubard y el Dr. Bracho en construir un par de nuevos 4-politpos quirales en el espacio de 4 dimensiones. Para esto, estudió a profundidad algunos 4-politopos estrellados regulares de dicho espacio y les aplicó una serie de operaciones para obtener poliedros quirales. Después, logró encontrar isometrías que lo han ayudado a extender los poliedros a 4-politopos quirales. Así, se encuentra escribiendo sus resultados para poder titularse de la maestría a la brevedad."

records.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
records.venue: Discrete Mathematics; arXiv:1608.07993
records.how_found: WebSearch; Semantic Scholar citations of Pellicer 2017; PDF extracted
records.relevance: Formulates the classification of full-rank chiral polytopes as an open problem (Problem 20) and records that only BHP 2014 (finite, E^4) and Pellicer (infinite, E^3) were known.
records.verbatim_quote: "Regular polytopes of full rank were classified in [46, Theorem 11.2], where it is also stated that there are no chiral polytopes of full rank. This claim turned out to be false; there are both finite chiral 4-polytopes in E4 [5] and infinite 4-polytopes in E3 [66]. It is natural now to ask for the classification of full rank chiral polytopes. Problem 20. Describe all chiral polytopes of full rank."

BOTTOM LINE (searches through 2026-09-07): no published finite chiral 4-polytope in E^4 or S^3 (chiral polytope of full rank, rank 4) other than Roli's cube (Bracho-Hubard-Pellicer, DCG 52 (2014)) was found in arXiv, zbMATH, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, DBLP, Google Scholar, or the UNAM thesis repository. Every 2014-2026 source that discusses full-rank chirality (Pellicer 2017 AMC; Cunningham-Pellicer open problems 2018, Problem 20; Pellicer BAG 2021; Pellicer DM 2021; Monson ADAM 2022; Hubard-Schulte arXiv 2604.00185, March 2026) cites Roli's cube as the only finite rank-4 example. The rank-5 example (Pellicer 2021) is infinite. Monson (2021/22): 'these objects do seem to be elusive.'

TWO UNPUBLISHED ITEMS ARE THE LIVE COMPETITION for the research question: (i) J. Bracho, D. González-Casanova, I. Hubard, 'Two new chiral 4-polytopes of full rank' -- listed as 'In preparation' in Hubard-Schulte's bibliography (arXiv 2604.00185, ref. [1], 31 Mar 2026); the PAPIIT IN109023 report (updated 2 Jul 2025) confirms the route (regular star 4-polytopes -> operations -> chiral polyhedra -> extension by isometries), consistent with paper (C)'s {12/(1,5),3,5} and {12/(1,5),3,5/2} with facets H_1({5,3,5/2}), H_0({5,3,5/2}). No thesis is deposited in the UNAM repository under González Casanova's name on this topic. (ii) I. Hubard, B. Trejo, 'A family of skeletal chiral 3- and 4-polytopes in R^4', cited as 'Preprint' (same bibliography, ref. [31]); Trejo's PhD thesis 'Chiral polytopes in Euclidian 4-space' (UNAM, in progress per Hubard's site); Trejo's June 2023 SiCGT talk 'A family of chiral polyhedra with helical faces in R4'. The PAPIIT report states Trejo classified the chiral skeletal polyhedra whose 1-skeleton lies in the graph of a regular convex 4-polytope (exactly 4 examples) and that the group 'determined which of them can be extended' to chiral 4-polytopes in E^4, with a paper 'to be submitted shortly'. This is the closest known work to the audited question (PETCOX polyhedra H_alpha(T) as facets, T convex regular); whether it covers H_0({5,3,3}) (type {30/(1,11),3}) and whether the extension exists could not be verified -- the preprint is not online. Neither item has appeared on arXiv, Google Scholar, DBLP or the UNAM repository as of the access date.

VERIFIED FACET CLAIM: PETCOX author PDF (matem.unam.mx/~roli/.../PetrieCoxeterFinal2.pdf), p.25: 'The type of H_alpha({5,3,3}) is {30/(1,11),3}, and for alpha=0 no vertices identify, so that H0({5,3,3}) can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope, but not H1({5,3,3}) in which four vertices come together.' The paper does not construct that 4-polytope; the phrase is an assertion without proof or reference. p.23: H_0({4,3,3}) 'was taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope in S3 (or R4) in [3]'.
